title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff to prevent regional failover thrashing under pressure
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Under sustained regional pressure we observed the SLO enforcer entering a backoff/failover thrashing loop that caused cascading regional failovers and excessive load shedding. This was triggered by a race in the backoff/hysteresis update path which allowed multiple concurrent adjustments to push a region into aggressive penalization without proper smoothing. The symptoms were high failover churn, increased tail latency for routed requests, and customer-facing error spikes. This PR implements a targeted hotfix with the following goals: 1) ensure atomic, monotonic backoff updates per-region; 2) add smoothing and minimum hold time to avoid oscillation; 3) emit new metrics to make regressions observable; 4) add unit + integration tests and a canary rollout plan. What changed (high level): atomicized backoff updates using per-region mutex and versioned token, introduce a backoff_smoothing factor and min_hold_seconds to enforce hysteresis, cap backoff increment rate to avoid rapid escalation, move the order of metric emission to after state is stabilized to avoid transient alerting, and add a safety valve that temporarily disables regional failover when we detect thrashing beyond threshold (configurable and off by default). Also added more robust tests that simulate concurrent enforcer updates and an e2e canary config. Testing: unit tests cover the new rate-limit and hold-time behavior (slo/enforcer/backoff_test.go). Integration tests simulate multi-region load and verify the enforcer stabilizes without oscillation. CI initially had a flaky e2e; the test was fixed and rerun. We also ran a staged canary in us-west-2 for 1 hour with synthetic load; no regressions observed and failover churn reduced to baseline. Rollout and mitigation: merged to main and rolled out as a canary to 10% of host groups for 2 hours, then 100% after health window. A rollback patch is prepared (revert-hotfix-161999) and can be applied if we observe any unexpected behavior. Observability: new metrics slo_enforcer.backoff_level, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_state, slo_enforcer.thrashing_detector_count and dashboards/alerts updated. Notes: this is a minimal/targeted hotfix focused on stability; additional follow-ups planned to refactor the enforcer state machine and to add stronger formal invariants (ENG-2345).
commit_summary: atomicize region backoff updates with mutex and version token
add backoff_smoothing, min_hold_seconds, and increment rate cap
safety valve to pause regional failovers on detected thrashing
emit new metrics and update dashboards/alerts
add unit and integration tests; fix flaky e2e test
canary deployment config and rollout script
changed_files: slo/enforcer/backoff.go - implement atomic backoff updates, smoothing, hold-time, rate cap
slo/enforcer/backoff_test.go - new concurrency and hysteresis tests
slo/enforcer/metrics.go - metrics for backoff_level and thrashing_detector
observability/alerts/slo-enforcer.yaml - adjust alert thresholds to use smoothed metric
cmd/slo-enforcer/main.go - add new runtime flag to enable safety valve
review_comments: Rohit Mehta: LGTM overall; please ensure the default min_hold_seconds is conservative (>=30s) to avoid impacting short spikes.
Sofia Martinez: Can you add a short note in README about the safety valve config and the expected behavior when it triggers?
Ethan Park: Unit tests look good but the concurrency test was flaky locally; I suggested increasing the wait window and adding deterministic seeding.
Aisha Khan (author): Addressed feedback - min_hold_seconds default set to 45s, added README section, and made concurrency test deterministic by using a test clock.
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff to prevent regional failover thrashing. Adds smoothing, hold time, rate caps, safety valve, and observability improvements. Recommended to monitor slo_enforcer.thrashing_detector_count post-deploy.
